summary.locked_model: Unchanged: sum of split (asymmetric) pseudo-Voigt peaks on a SNIP background, auto-detected. Split-PV already captures the sharp-peak asymmetry seen in the 10.3–11.6 and 21.6–22.8 zoom windows; the shoulder/knee near ~26.2 in the 25.6–26.9 window is handled by the multi-component global fit with adequate prominence (a second component if auto-detect resolves it).

detailed_analysis: In-situ VT powder XRD of sodium ibuprofen dihydrate heated under N2 (5-45 deg 2theta, Cu Kalpha) was fit at six temperatures (28.7-65.7C) with a uniform split pseudo-Voigt + SNIP model, all achieving global R2~0.9994-0.9995. The dominant, well-constrained finding is a discontinuous dehydration phase transition centered near 44.6C. Below the transition (28.7-40.9C) the pattern is dominated by hydrate reflections (strong ~11.0 and ~22.2 deg); above it (55.8-65.7C) these vanish entirely and a distinct product reflection set (~11.9, ~15.95, ~19.99 deg) dominates. Index 3 (48.3C) is a genuine coexistence frame (product fraction 0.735) showing both phases. The order parameter built from integrated areas is monotonic and model-robust (product fraction 0.067->0.067->0.097->0.735->1.0->1.0), providing the clearest transition signature. Peak positions are essentially static within each phase, ruling out continuous lattice expansion as the dominant effect; the reflection-count drop (27-28 to 17-22) reflects the product having a different, fewer-reflection cell rather than detection noise, because the count change coincides exactly with the area crossover. Crystallite-size reporting is not interpretable here: instrumental FWHM was set to 0 so all Scherrer sizes are lower bounds, the mean-size-vs-T trend is essentially flat/noisy (R2=0.08), no Williamson-Hall analysis was run, and per-peak sizes span >3x in the transition frames, consistent with mixed-phase broadening where an isotropic mean is an oversimplification. A few fitted components in indices 3-5 are physically dubious (FWHM 0.066 deg -> Scherrer 123 nm; a peak with amplitude ~1e-7 and FWHM 0.12 deg; several eta pinned at 0 or 1), and should be disregarded as unconstrained/cosmetic rather than treated as physical. The next logical step is phase identification (structure_matching/xrd) on the low-T and high-T end members to assign the hydrate and anhydrous/product structures, passing in the refined FWHMs.

scientific_claims.claim: Sodium ibuprofen dihydrate undergoes a discontinuous dehydration phase transition centered near 44.6C under N2, evidenced by disappearance of hydrate reflections (~11.0, ~22.2 deg) and growth of a distinct product reflection set (~11.9, ~15.95, ~19.99 deg), with two-phase coexistence at 48.3C and a sigmoidal area-based product fraction (0.07->0.10->0.74->1.0).
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: Locates the dehydration temperature and demonstrates a first-order (coexistence) rather than continuous transformation, which is directly relevant to processing, storage stability, and solid-form control of a pharmaceutical salt.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone determined the dehydration transition temperature and mechanism (coexistence vs continuous) of sodium ibuprofen dihydrate under inert atmosphere by in-situ powder XRD?

flagged_spectra_analysis.summary: No spectra were flagged; all six fits reached global R2~0.9994-0.9995 with only irreducible sharp-apex residuals on the most intense peaks (~11.0, ~22.2 deg), accepted as the split-PV profile limit.
flagged_spectra_analysis.scientific_significance: Uniformly high fit quality across the series means the observed transition is a real data feature, not a fit-quality artifact.

refit_analysis.summary: No spectra were adaptively refitted; a single split pseudo-Voigt + SNIP model was applied unchanged to all six temperatures.
refit_analysis.scientific_implications: Because one model form fit every frame, the reflection appearance/disappearance and area redistribution reflect genuine phase evolution rather than a model switch, supporting the dehydration-transition interpretation and weakening any detection-artifact explanation.

=== Dehydration phase-transition analysis ===
Temperatures (C): [28.7, 35.9, 40.9, 48.3, 55.8, 65.7]
Number of reflections: [27, 28, 27, 22, 17, 18]
Detected transition between index 2 (40.9 C) and 3 (48.3 C); midpoint ~44.6 C
Hydrate ~11 deg area: [288555.3, 289483.7, 274774.5, 83225.7, 0.0, 0.0]
Product ~20 deg area: [20672.4, 20683.2, 29637.9, 230817.2, 308883.6, 309958.0]
Product fraction: [0.067, 0.067, 0.097, 0.735, 1.0, 1.0]

hydrate_area_11deg.interpretation: Loss of the dihydrate phase; holds ~288k through 40.9C then collapses to 0 above the transition, marking dehydration.

product_area_20deg.interpretation: Growth of the anhydrous/product phase; rises sharply across 44.6C and saturates at ~309k, complementary to hydrate loss.

product_fraction.interpretation: Sigmoidal two-state order parameter (0.07,0.07,0.10,0.74,1.0,1.0); step between 40.9 and 48.3C defines the transition with coexistence at 48.3C.

reflection_count.interpretation: Drops from 27-28 to 17-22 after ~44C, consistent with the product having a different, fewer-reflection unit cell rather than detection noise.

diagnostic_peak_positions.interpretation: Positions are static within each phase (hydrate ~22.2 deg, product ~20 deg), indicating whole-phase replacement rather than continuous lattice thermal expansion.

mean_crystallite_size.interpretation: Scattered 26-31.6 nm with negligible slope (R2=0.08); not interpretable because instrumental FWHM=0 (sizes are lower bounds) and transition frames mix two phases.

caveats: Instrumental FWHM was set to 0, so all Scherrer sizes are lower bounds and the mean-size-vs-T trend (R2=0.08) is not interpretable; no Williamson-Hall analysis was performed. Per-peak sizes span >3x in the transition frames, consistent with mixed-phase broadening, so an isotropic Scherrer mean is an oversimplification. Several fitted components in indices 3-5 are unconstrained/cosmetic (e.g. FWHM 0.066 deg -> 123 nm; amplitude ~1e-7; eta pinned at 0 or 1) and must not be treated as physical. Crystalline phases are not yet identified; structure_matching/xrd on the low-T and high-T end members (passing refined FWHMs) is needed to assign the hydrate and anhydrous/product structures and confirm the transition assignment. The transition temperature (~44.6C) is bracketed only between 40.9 and 48.3C by the available sampling; finer temperature steps would sharpen it.

locked_fitting_config.analysis_approach: Run a single global full-pattern fit per frame with fit_pattern (SNIP background, auto peak detection, split pseudo-Voigt line shape), fitting the full 5-45 deg range. Because peak positions and the whole reflection set change markedly across temperature, the series is split into distinct structural regimes (dihydrate → transforming → dehydrated phase). Track peak positions, intensities, FWHMs and the appearance/disappearance of reflections across the series to locate and characterize the dehydration phase transition. Keep auto-detection ON every frame (do NOT freeze centers) so relocated/new peaks are captured.
locked_fitting_config.physical_model: Unchanged: sum of split (asymmetric) pseudo-Voigt peaks on a SNIP background, auto-detected. Split-PV already captures the sharp-peak asymmetry seen in the 10.3–11.6 and 21.6–22.8 zoom windows; the shoulder/knee near ~26.2 in the 25.6–26.9 window is handled by the multi-component global fit with adequate prominence (a second component if auto-detect resolves it).
locked_fitting_config.fitting_strategy: Keep the single global fit_pattern per frame (method='snip', snip_iterations='auto', model='split pseudo-Voigt', auto peak detection via prominence_frac, auto-detect ON every frame — do NOT freeze centers). Change only the low-angle bound: inspect the establishing (28.7 C) frame and set lo where the steep descent flattens into ordinary background — approximately fit_range=(6.0, 45.0), positioned below the ~7–8 deg reflections but above the descending air-scatter tail; verify by re-fitting and confirming a structureless low-angle residual and recovery of the full ~12–18 reflection set (if the low-angle residual is still oscillatory or only a handful of peaks are found, lo is still inside the climb — raise it and re-fit). Fix one window on the establishing frame and reuse it on every frame in the series. Accept on peak_region_r2 >= 0.90 (read global r_squared as context; a low-SNR gap with structureless residual accepts, a peaked residual = unmodelled reflection → lower prominence_frac/min_distance_deg and re-run the single global fit). Do NOT re-fit individual peaks with symmetric fit_profile. Treat systematic VT position shifts (e.g. 11.0→11.9, 22.2→20.0 deg) as physically real phase/lattice changes to be tracked, not displacement error. Pass instrumental_fwhm_deg=0.0 and report Scherrer sizes as lower bounds; size/strain secondary to phase tracking.
